Q2: Section 3.2/Table 3 report that WFG coupling (aerated fertigation) extended the time to Dra = 75% for all five emitters (3-29%); Section 3.4/Fig. 5-6 report that Cu and Us were higher under WFG coupling than under non-aerated fertigation for every emitter; Fig. 4 shows blocked emitters appear later and are more uniformly distributed along the tape. Q3: Reduced clogging under aeration is shown both by emitter flow-rate measurements (Dra, Section 3.1-3.3) and independently by SEM observation of clogging material (Section 3.5.1), which found thinner, less dense deposits with less adhesion under WFG coupling. Q4: Section 3.5 measures the intermediate variables (micromorphology of clogging material by SEM; microbial community by MiSeq sequencing, Fig. 8-9, showing decreased Betaproteobacteriales/Chitinophagales/Myxococcales and increased Cytophagales etc.), and Fig. 6 links uniformity (Cu, Us) to the degree of clogging (Dra). Q8: Conclusions state the controlled conditions may not reflect real-world variation in water quality, system configuration and crop irrigation regimes, and that clogging is influenced by water source, configuration and crop type.

Lab bench with 100 m tapes, no farm/scheme scale (Q6 no). No SD, CI or range reported for Dra, service-life extension or Cu/Us; only R2/p-values of regressions and pre-test Cv of emitters (Q9 no). evidence: Q1: Sections 2.5-2.8 and 3 - the authors run their own WEAP and AquaCrop model simulations for the Chichaoua-Mejjate basin under five RCMs and ten management/climate scenarios to 2050, and report their own projected net precipitation, crop water demand, unmet demand and aquifer balance results.
